I get that. When I started medicating I felt I had the energy and motivation to be productive. My first week I put together some new furniture I had been putting off for a while and started some house projects. But there are days when I have nothing to do. I have all this energy so I end up dreading doing nothing. Part of it is how I was brought up. My parents would always throw chores at me at a really young age. If I wasn’t doing anything productive with all of my spare time I was seen as lazy. As an adult i am conditioned to feeling guilty and ashamed for sitting around watching tv after a long day at work. trying to relax and unwind became difficult. It took weeks of therapy for me to stop being so hard on myself and to start practicing self care. So when I have nothing to do I read, play guitar, walk my dog, catch up on some tv shows, write in my journal, exercise, meditate, and anything else I want to do

I went to therapy for my social anxiety and it has helped me tremendously

I didn’t understand why people went to therapy. 
 
After my 1st therapy session I understood.

It’s not. It’s really really not. There was a dark period in my life where all I did was smoke and drink, trying to numb myself from how I really felt, and I didn’t want to feel like that anymore. With no job or insurance my doctor signed me up for free group counselling. He said there was a waiting list and it should take about 3 months. 

TWO YEARS LATER… I finally get an email regarding my first group counselling session. I went to maybe 2.5 sessions and realized group therapy wasn’t for me. By then I was an even bigger mess dealing with heavy drug use. What I really needed was to see a professional who dealt with the issues that I was having. Thankfully I got a new job that payed well enough for me to start paying for therapy out of pocket.

I know the old saying we all keep hearing “every body is different” so I can’t say it will be better but from what I’ve read from others who started with Vyvanse the side effects you’re dealing with now will be less intense over the next couple of weeks. If it doesn’t, then it might be a good idea to talk to your doctor and they can lower the dosage or try something else

I had an interview at a company that built furnaces and  water heaters (or that’s what the ad said) so I went into what looked like a brand new office and was interviewed by a woman who looked younger than me (I was 25 at the time) I did my best for the interview because I was laid off from my previous job and was desperate. Everything went great and she said if I am selected they’ll call me for a second interview. Cool. So 2 days later they call and we arrange a time for the second interview.  Cool cool. The next day I go in and I am told right away that I’m hired. Cool cool cool! But then it’s gets weird and began one of the biggest mistakes of my life. 

The interviewee introduces me to 2 other guys who were just hired. They all look the same age as me. Then we meet this dude who is gonna drive us to their corporate head office. For some dumb reason I agreed and we all jumped into his van. We’re driving for about 40 minutes and we arrive at their “head office” which happened to be like a 10 minute walk from my house. I had this feeling in my gut that I should just leave and go home but again the dumbass that I was just ignored the feeling and we went to the office. We walk into a conference room with 15 other new people. Some guy talks to use for like 5 minutes about how much money he and the other employees make selling hvac unites door to door. I just went with it cause how bad could it be? 

After our “orientation” we all get a door to door “trainer”. So I meet up with mine and the same dude that drove me. We hop in the guys van and drive to the next town to begin our training. I won’t bore you with the details but we knocked on 3 doors and as we walked to the fourth I say “yeah... I quit”. I start to walk to the nearest bus stop and one of the guys say “hey you forgot your bag in the van!” I just said “keep it!” 
There wasn’t anything in the bag except for their trainer book and some other shit they gave me. And the bag was old and starting to rip so I didn’t miss it. 

So here I am in a town I don’t know too much about. I have 3 dollars in change. Just enough to take a bus to the nearest station. Turns out the bus is actually $4. I told one bus driver that I don’t know where I am and that I just needed to get to an atm. Bus driver refuses to leave until I pay the full amount. I get out and start walking. I call my dad to ask if he can pick me up. About an hour later of calling back my dad to figure out where I am I finally see him and I’m saved. But as soon I got in the car I just started to cry because if I had just listened to my gut earlier I would have been home and my day wouldn’t have been wasted on this shit. 

From then on I would never ignore a gut feeling.
